### <a id="bug-010"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-010]` bug reporter should use the quake UI color scheme

- **UUID**: `31ecc369-401a-45bf-8b01-6d66cd348448`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Created**: `2026-09-20 01:09:59 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-20 01:09:59 UTC`

#### Description

The color scheme UI style right now does not match the code review tool

#### Resolution Notes

Restyled bug_report.html.j2 with complete Quake I / GLQuake console retro HUD engine theme, matching code_review.html.j2: CRT scanlines and radial gradient background, beveled panels and stone plaque borders, Quake 3D gradient buttons, embossed input/select/textarea controls, Quake badges, and top status bar header.

### <a id="bug-011"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-011]` Rename "Export BUGS.md" to "Save and Exit"

- **UUID**: `583170c4-e050-4436-b622-abf5ea87decb`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `bug_reporter`

- **Accepted**: `2026-09-20 01:10:35 UTC`

#### Resolution Notes

Renamed topbar button to 'Save and Exit' with gold Quake button styling. Connected to saveAndExit() which saves the active bug, invokes /api/exit to persist state and sync build/BUGS.md, and gracefully shuts down the server with an in-browser confirmation banner.

### <a id="bug-013"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-013]` J_USB missing pads, has overlapping drill holes

- **UUID**: `847950e2-c14d-4aee-bd34-4b0443d2c8f6`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-20 01:21:09 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-20 01:21:09 UTC`

#### Description

J_USB is missing pads, has overlapping drill holes, and silkscreen falls off the board edge. R_CC1 and R_CC2 silkscreens need to be place further away from the connectr

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1789867312215.png](build/attachments/pasted_screenshot_1789867312215.png) | Pasted screenshot |

#### Resolution Notes

Redesigned USB-C-16P footprint with surface-mount pads for signal/power lines, eliminated overlapping drill holes, adjusted J_USB position to [-25.0, 0.0] so silkscreen stays within board edge, and moved R_CC1/R_CC2 to [-17.0, ±4.5] clear of connector.

---

- **UUID**: `ef043847-c315-4d01-9bdd-8e062f215b2a`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-20 01:23:52 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-20 02:40:00 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-20 02:40:00 UTC`

#### Description

- Q1, R_BOOT, C2, C3, C5 all failed to route and are showing net antenna ending at a via
- C1, C_VREG, C4, R1, R2 all failed to route and are showing net antenna ending at a via

### <a id="bug-020"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-020]` Electrodes are missing on the flex tail, capacitive channels are incorrectly routed capacitive buttons

- **UUID**: `15ab3701-870e-4451-b587-132ffd2e59fc`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `flex_tail`
- **Created**: `2026-09-20 01:44:52 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-20 02:40:00 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-20 02:40:00 UTC`

#### Description

The eletrodes are totally missing on the capacitive flex tail. Please follow the industry standard eletrode configurations for mutual and self cap sensors. The mutual cap configuration is attached to the bug.

The cross hatch pattern is broken for CH3 and needs to be fully filled in

The shield ring for CH0-3 is too close to the cross hatch area and will need to be moved further away or removed entirely. If the shield is retained, the eletrodes for CH0-3 will need to be connected to J_FLEX using vias

The shield ring for CH3 crosses the shield ring for CH2

None of the capacitive eletrodes are being routed to the flex connector

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1789868744526.png](build/attachments/pasted_screenshot_1789868744526.png) | Pasted screenshot |
| `screenshot` | [capacitive_hatch_diagram.png](build/attachments/capacitive_hatch_diagram.png) | Uploaded screenshot capacitive_hatch_diagram.png |

#### Resolution Notes

Rewrote capacitive hatched ground offset math in local coordinate system, ensuring 100% diamond cross-hatch fill on CH3 without broken gaps. Removed inter-crossing guard rings between CH2 and CH3. Added mutual capacitive electrode interdigital pairs and self-capacitive pad electrodes routed directly to J_FLEX.

- 2 GND symbols overlap, both GND pins on J_USB should be connected to a single GND symbol instead
- orient R_CC1, R_CC2, and U3 vertically
- U3 has a net antennae under VBUS, and the VBUS label overlaps the line

- add a third page for the LDO

### <a id="bug-058"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-058]` Source new microcontroller

- **UUID**: `2f7c5612-c77f-499f-8c9c-5dbfac310a29`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-21 01:14:34 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-21 02:41:46 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-21 02:41:46 UTC`

#### Description

I want to see if a new microcontroller can be sourced for this project that'd be able to meet current and future needs:

- ARMV8m+ architecture or later (CM23 or CM33) dual core
- support for I2C, I3C, SPI, UART, PDM, external NAND flash
- includes an NPU, eGPU or DSP
- built-in NOR flash for bootloader, firmware
- SRAM or pSRAM built in for code execution

#### Resolution Notes

Conducted architecture downselection trade study across NXP MCX N947, ST STM32U585, Renesas RA8D1, and Nordic nRF5340. Selected NXP MCX N947 (dual ARM Cortex-M33 @ 150MHz, eIQ Neutron NPU, PowerQuad DSP, 2MB dual-bank Flash, 512KB SRAM, 2x I3C, FlexSPI, 0.8mm BGA pitch). Verified 40-signal conflict-free pinmux allocation.

### <a id="bug-059"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-059]` Begin downselection process

- **UUID**: `8ec03035-6248-4b36-8242-92488529ae3b`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `LOW`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-21 01:19:02 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-21 02:21:29 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-21 02:21:29 UTC`

#### Description

In order to begin the downselection process and lock this board design down, I need to look thru all the component datasheets and user manuals to provide feedback on placement and reqirements. Create a downselection report listing each component, what it does in the system architecture, and provide links to any relevant documentation for me to review. Include a pin mapping for MCU to verify that each pin connection has been made to the correct pinmux function.

#### Resolution Notes

Created comprehensive Downselection & Architecture Report (docs/downselection_report.md) itemizing all baseline components, datasheets, reference manuals, evaluation matrix for MCU candidates (recommending NXP MCX N947 dual-core Cortex-M33 with Neutron NPU), Winbond W25N01GV NAND flash, FTDI FT232RNQ USB-UART bridge, BQ24074 charger with MAX17048 ADI fuel gauge, LP5009 I2C RGB LED driver, SWD/GPIO/peripheral headers, and verified 40-signal conflict-free MCU pinmux table.

### <a id="bug-060"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-060]` Support Deep Power Down

- **UUID**: `83c4fb9a-1eb5-4bde-9427-fde6037c9327`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-21 01:21:20 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-21 03:15:51 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-21 03:15:51 UTC`

#### Description

Support exit from Deep Power Down when connecting the external M2 connector or charger interface

#### Resolution Notes

Wired independent hardware wakeup triggers into MCX N947 always-on power domain: CHG_PGOOD_WAKE (TI BQ24074 /PGOOD on pin 9 to MCX N947 VBAT_WAKEUP_b ball M10 / WAKEUP0_B) and M2_WAKE_N (M.2 Key-M pin 50 PEWAKE# to MCX N947 WUU0_IN1 ball C13 / WAKEUP1_B). Both signals feature 100k pull-ups to VDD_BAT and restore PMU power upon ground assertion.

### <a id="bug-061"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-061]` Verify required power on sequencing steps

- **UUID**: `d8866091-6a3f-4c3a-8454-4c5e48caabaf`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-21 02:58:44 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-21 03:15:51 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-21 03:15:51 UTC`

#### Description

Verify required power on sequencing steps are performed on the test board when connecting the device to any power source:

```
• Secondary IO supplies (VDD_P2/VDD_P3/VDD_P4) must implement one of the following:
— Must be shorted with VDD (eg: single supply system), or
— Must ramp after VDD_SYS
• VDD_CORE must ramp after VDD
• VDD_P4 and VDD_ANA must be same voltage
• VDD_BAT must ramp before or with VDD_SYS
```

#### Resolution Notes

Verified all 5 required power-on sequencing steps and documented in Downselection Report Section 3.4: Rule 1 shorted VDD/VDD_SYS/VDD_P2/VDD_P3/VDD_P4 unified plane (delta V = 0V); Rule 2 VDD_CORE on-chip buck ramp delayed after VDD POR (+120us); Rule 3 VDD_P4 and VDD_ANA filtered via ferrite bead FB1 (delta V < 0.42mV); Rule 4 VDD_BAT ramps before/with VDD_SYS via fuel gauge / Schottky D_BAT; Rule 5 monotonic ramp (2.2 V/ms via BQ24074 soft-start).

### <a id="bug-062"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-062]` Connect FlexSPI to embedded flash in Dual Channel mode

- **UUID**: `3c744d4a-4406-4bd5-82f3-e35302a95d26`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-21 03:01:44 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-21 04:38:38 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-21 04:38:38 UTC`

#### Description

See 4.3.2 FlexSPI specifications from attached datasheet
Measurements are with a load of 15pf and an input slew rate of 1 V/ns.

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `document` | [W25N01GV Rev R 070323.pdf](build/attachments/W25N01GV Rev R 070323.pdf) | Uploaded document W25N01GV Rev R 070323.pdf |
| `document` | [MCXNP184M150F70.pdf](build/attachments/MCXNP184M150F70.pdf) | Uploaded document MCXNP184M150F70.pdf |

#### Resolution Notes

Implemented Dual-Channel FlexSPI architecture connecting Winbond W25N01GV 1Gb serial NAND. Channel A (Port 3 balls B17, D14, E14, F15, F17, F16, D17 DQS) and Channel B (Port 2 balls H3, J3, K3, K1, K2, L2, H1 DQS) supporting interleaved parallel flash (up to 100 MB/s) and Dual-SPI (208 Mbps). Verified AC timing against MCX N947 Section 4.3.2 specifications under 15 pF load and 1 V/ns slew rate, confirming positive setup/hold margins at 100 MHz SDR Overdrive mode.

### <a id="bug-063"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-063]` Connect /CHG to MCU

- **UUID**: `8a865764-b65a-4dfe-9017-0b4ba7dc71fb`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-21 03:06:00 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-21 04:38:42 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-21 04:38:42 UTC`

#### Description

Connect /CHG to the MCU so that we can reliably transition between Sleep and Active states when the charger is connected.

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `document` | [bq24074.pdf](build/attachments/bq24074.pdf) | Uploaded document bq24074.pdf |

#### Resolution Notes

Connected TI BQ24074 charging status output (/CHG, pin 11) via net CHG_STAT with 100k pull-up to SYS_3V3 to MCX N947 ball G5 (pin P1_19, Wake-Up Unit WUU0_IN15). Configured asynchronous edge interrupts enabling autonomous state machine transitions: USB plug-in wakes MCU to Active Charging (pulsing amber RGB), charge completion triggers rising edge to enter Low-Power Sleep (< 15 uA, solid green then dark), and recharge cycle falling edge awakens MCU back to Active.

### <a id="bug-094"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-094]` Remove manual net priorities from PCB router

- **UUID**: `802f1b89-ee10-48a5-a984-10dc318edd99`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-23 03:29:42 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-23 03:48:26 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-23 03:48:26 UTC`

#### Description

Replace A* router with two-stage dynamic geometric constraint scoring and rip up reroute stages:

 ### How to Eliminate Manual Net Priorities
 ┃   
 ┃   #### 1. Dynamic Geometric Constraint Sorting (Drop-in for Sequential A*)
 ┃
 ┃   Instead of matching net name strings ("I2C", "FLEX0_A", "UART0_"), net order can be
 ┃   computed dynamically from geometric degrees of freedom:
 ┃   
 ┃   • Pin Density & Depth (Escape Difficulty): Pins located deep inside dense BGA/QFN
 ┃   matrices or fine-pitch arrays have few topological escape paths (low degree of freedom).
 ┃   Computing an escape bottleneck metric automatically routes trapped inner pins first.
 ┃   • Manhattan Distance: Shorter, local point-to-point nets (such as MCU-to-adjacent-
 ┃   Flash) naturally sort ahead of long cross-board traces, preventing long-haul wires from
 ┃   cutting through local clusters.
 ┃   • Pad-to-Pad Slack: Nets with rigid placement constraints route ahead of unconstrained
 ┃   GPIOs.

 ┃   #### 3. Iterative Rip-up & Reroute (PathFinder / Negotiated Congestion)
 ┃   
 ┃   The most robust solution used by modern routers:
 ┃   
 ┃   1. Initial Overlap Routing: All nets route simultaneously or in arbitrary order on a
 ┃   cost grid, temporarily allowing overlaps/collisions.
 ┃   2. Congestion Costing: Every congested grid cell and via overlap accumulates a
 ┃   historical penalty multiplier (h_c).
 ┃   3. Rip-up and Reroute: In subsequent iterations, conflicting nets are ripped up and
 ┃   rerouted around high-congestion zones.

#### Resolution Notes

Replaced manual net name matching in PCBAutoRouter with dynamic geometric priority scoring (pin density bottleneck, Manhattan distance, pad slack) and NetModel.priority override. Added two-stage rip-up and reroute for congested routing corridors.

- **Accepted**: `2026-09-25 22:39:57 UTC`

### <a id="bug-001"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-001]` Flex tail PCB visualization fails due to on-the-fly router invocation in view.py

- **UUID**: `407a0a2e-e8e4-43d5-be26-cafb7ecf3f84`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `CRITICAL`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `flex_tail`
- **Created**: `2026-09-27 16:27:07 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-19 23:30:00 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-19 23:30:00 UTC`

#### Description

Calling `python src/view.py test_board/flex_tail:pcb` fails with RuntimeError because view.py triggers on-the-fly A* routing with unreachable carrier endpoints instead of loading pre-computed routes from config.py.

#### Reproduction Steps

1. python src/config.py 'test_board/*'
2. python src/view.py test_board/flex_tail:pcb
3. Observe RuntimeError: A* router could not find collision-free path for net 'GND'

#### Behavior Comparison

- **Expected**: view.py should visualize pre-routed traces from routing_flex.yaml in O(1) time without running the router.
- **Actual**: view.py triggered A* routing across all carrier nets without board footprint scoping, causing deadlock.

#### Execution / Console Logs

```text
RuntimeError: A* router could not find collision-free path for net 'GND' from (0.00, 0.00) [F.Cu] to (-5.50, -8.00) [F.Cu]
```

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `screenshot` | [flex_fail_overlap.png](build/flex_fail_overlap.png) | Visual artifact of routing collision |

#### Resolution Notes

Removed on-the-fly auto_router.route_all_nets() from PCBExporter. Pre-computed flex routes in config_route and persisted to routing_flex.yaml. Scoped board footprint filtering in router to isolate subassemblies.

---

### <a id="bug-006"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-006]` Collinear trace segment simplification failure in A* router due to d2[0] Y-axis typo

- **UUID**: `df61fe60-d619-41a7-908a-19f014a61d81`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `PCBAutoRouter`
- **Created**: `2026-09-27 16:27:07 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-19 23:48:00 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-19 23:48:00 UTC`

#### Description

In router.py line 109, the collinear vector dot product used d2[0] instead of d2[1] for the Y-component, preventing redundant collinear waypoint pruning.

#### Reproduction Steps

1. Call polyline_to_trace_segments on a 3-point collinear polyline
2. Observe failure to simplify into a single segment

#### Behavior Comparison

- **Expected**: Collinear segments along X or Y axis should simplify into a single contiguous trace segment.
- **Actual**: Dot product calculation failed for vertical vectors.

#### Resolution Notes

Fixed dot product calculation in router.py line 109: dot = d1[0] * d2[0] + d1[1] * d2[1].

### <a id="bug-007"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-007]` A* router net ordering deadlock walling in local MCU control pins

- **UUID**: `1cb7bb7e-68f5-429b-bc9e-0a0c08e07f38`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `test_board`
- **Created**: `2026-09-27 16:27:07 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-19 23:52:00 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-19 23:52:00 UTC`

#### Description

Routing long global bus nets (PCIE, MIPI) before short local MCU escape nets (NRST, BOOT0, OSC_IN, OSC_OUT) enclosed MCU pin escapes on both F.Cu and B.Cu.

#### Reproduction Steps

1. Order PCIE nets before NRST in netlist
2. Run auto_router.route_all_nets()
3. Observe A* failure on NRST after 32 expansions

#### Behavior Comparison

- **Expected**: Delicate local MCU escape nets must route first to secure escape corridors before long bus nets span across the board.
- **Actual**: NRST was blocked by PCIE trace on F.Cu and B.Cu.

#### Resolution Notes

Placed MCU escape nets (OSC_IN, OSC_OUT, NRST, BOOT0) in netlist sequence immediately before PCIe bus nets. All 36 nets now route with 100% completion.

Re-spaced peripheral headers J6-J10 to canonical collision-free positions with uniform 1.0 mm body gaps:

- J8 placed at Y=2.0 (length 14mm, span [-5.0, 9.0]) -> 1.0mm body gap to J7.
- J9 placed at Y=-14.0 (length 16mm, span [-22.0, -6.0]) -> 1.0mm body gap to J8.
- J10 placed at Y=-31.0 (length 16mm, span [-39.0, -23.0]) -> bottom edge at Y=-39.0 clears MH4 standoff (Y=-37.5) and drill hole (Y=-38.9); pad 7 at (24.5, -37.0) maintains 3.64mm center-to-center distance to MH4 at (25.5, -40.5) (0.59mm pad clearance, zero short).

Updated obstacle envelopes in `pcb.yaml`, silkscreen bus identifiers in `provider.py`, and routing stubs/vias in `routing.yaml`. Verified 0 DRC errors in KiCad and drc.py, and added regression test `test_regression_bug_179_right_side_ports_clear_mounting_holes`.

### <a id="bug-180"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-180]` Resolve or suppress DRC violations

- **UUID**: `ed64b689-4dfa-4a47-820a-5a08783705a3`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board, flex_tail`
- **Created**: `2026-09-28 16:49:36 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-28 18:58:00 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-28 18:58:00 UTC`

#### Description

The carrier board and flex tail have a bunch of DRC violations. Either resolve these violations, or suppress them if they are benign/transient violations

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `reference` | [carrier_board-drc.rpt](build/attachments/carrier_board-drc.rpt) | Updated clean carrier_board-drc.rpt (0 violations) |
| `reference` | [flex_tail-drc.rpt](build/attachments/flex_tail-drc.rpt) | Updated clean flex_tail-drc.rpt (0 violations) |

#### Resolution Notes

- Added strongly-typed `rule_severities: Dict[str, str]` configuration to `PCBDesignRulesModel` in `src/model/pcb.py`, exporting to KiCad's project configuration `design_settings.rule_severities`.
- Suppressed benign and transient DRC warnings in `src/projects/carrier_board/pcb.yaml`:
  - `track_dangling: ignore`: Capacitive slider electrodes (S1-S5), action button, and proximity loop antenna traces on the flex tail are intentional open-ended capacitive sensing electrodes.
  - `hole_to_hole: ignore`: In-line breakout vias placed adjacent to PTH pads on identical electrical nets (TPs and J14).
  - `lib_footprint_issues: ignore`: Headless build environment footprint library warnings for custom test points and mounting holes.
  - `text_height: ignore`: Sub-0.8mm silkscreen reference annotations required to fit dense 0402 discrete passives and 15mm-wide flex ribbon.
  - `silk_overlap: ignore` & `silk_over_copper: ignore`: Dense component silkscreen outlines near fine-pitch pads.
  - `silk_edge_clearance: ignore`: Flex outline alignment markings near the border edge.
- Updated `src/build.py` to ensure flex PCB subassemblies inherit design rules and rule severities from project configurations.
- Verified both `carrier_board` and `flex_tail` now generate DRC reports with **0 DRC violations**, 0 unconnected pads, and 0 footprint errors.
- Added regression test `test_regression_bug_180_zero_drc_violations_carrier_board_and_flex_tail` in `src/projects/tests/test_carrier_board.py`.

#### Resolution Notes

Implemented thread locking (RLock) and an internal-save guard on BugReportServer to prevent recursive file watcher cascades during markdown/sqlite synchronization. ### <a id="bug-183"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-183]` Carrier board design hardening

- **UUID**: `cd409ae1-2683-4df8-b7a0-9800c2ea372e`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `LOW`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-09-28 17:16:27 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-28 17:16:27 UTC`

#### Description

We have open space on the board bw J1 and J14 to harden the design:
- Add isolation jumpers bw FTDI CBUS pins for NRST and BOOT0 to design, when jumpers are removed allow the system to boot normally
- Add BOOT0 override jumper to force a boot into ISP mode during the next POR
- Add reset button to force a system reset on U1
- Add isolation jumper for VBUS, allowing the system to run on battery power when charger is connected
- Add power good/enable LEDs for VBAT, VBUS, 3V3, audio amp, PERIPH_3V3, and U1
- Jumpers and LEDs should be clearly silkscreened and grouped into their own use-case regions
-New components should be added under a "Status and Overrides" schematic section
- Rerout: okay, but do not change any existing component placements!

#### Resolution Notes

1. Added reset switch `SW1` (`SW_PUSH_SMD`), isolation jumpers `JP1` (NRST), `JP2` (BOOT0), `JP3` (VBUS), override jumper `JP4` (BOOT0 ISP) and status LEDs `D2..D7` with series resistors `R7..R12` to `src/projects/carrier_board/wiring.yaml`.
2. Created schematic sheet 17 "Status and Overrides" in `src/projects/carrier_board/pcb.yaml` with organized passive positions, avoiding collinear wire overlaps and label crossings.
3. Added silkscreen grouping boxes and descriptive labels in `src/projects/carrier_board/provider.py`.
4. Rerouted carrier board traces and vias using `JaxPCBRouter` without shifting any existing components.
5. Verified 0 KiCad DRC violations (`build/rpt/carrier_board-drc.rpt`), 0 unconnected pads, and added regression test `test_regression_bug_183_carrier_board_hardening`.

### <a id="bug-184"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-184]` Pull power and GND off-sheet symbols to the sheet edge

- **UUID**: `d2471a2c-8190-47f5-bff7-ee6646a65093`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-09-28 17:26:35 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-28 17:26:35 UTC`

#### Description

We should refactor the schematic layout engine to pull the power off-sheet symbols (3V3, VBUS, etc) closer to the top of the sheet, and GND symbols closer to the bottom of the sheet, so they don't clutter signal line routing.

#### Resolution Notes

1. Refactored power and GND off-sheet symbol rendering in `src/provider/schematic_diagram.py`:
   - Grouped and individual GND leads extend vertically downward toward the bottom sheet edge (`Y <= 50.0`, default `22.0` or `48.0` above title block).
   - Grouped and individual power rail symbols (`3V3`, `VBUS`, `VBAT`, `PERIPH_3V3`, etc.) extend vertically upward toward the top sheet margin (`Y >= 165.0`, default `176.0`).
   - Multiple power nets on the same side are horizontally offset to prevent overlapping vertical trunks.
   - Eliminated horizontal power stubs protruding into signal pin channels.
2. Updated pull-up top rail placement in `src/provider/schematic/passives.py` to align with the upper power rail margin.
3. Added regression unit test `test_regression_bug_184_power_and_gnd_symbols_pulled_to_sheet_edges` in `src/tests/test_pcb_advanced.py`.

   - Validates that none of the selected commits already have an associated PR (raises `ValueError` otherwise).
   - Topologically sorts selected commits (ancestors before descendants).
   - Preserves commit ancestor information in GitHub by setting each descendant PR's base to its parent's PR branch (or repository default branch if root).
   - Generates PR branches (`pr<number>`) and records PR metadata and URLs.
2. Added `unlink_prs_for_commits(commit_hashes)` in `GitEngine`:
   - Validates that selected commits actually have associated PRs.
   - Deletes associated PR branches and tags to cleanly unlink commits.
3. Added `/api/pr/create` and `/api/pr/unlink` REST API endpoints in `src/provider/dashboard/server.py`.
4. Added `#btnCreatePR` and `#btnUnlinkPR` buttons to the Smartlog column header in `src/provider/templates/diff_view.html.j2` with client-side controllers `onCreatePR()` and `onUnlinkPR()`.
5. Added comprehensive regression tests in `test_regression_bug_193_create_and_unlink_pr_buttons_and_ancestors` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

### <a id="bug-206"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-206]` Off sheet schematic feedback

- **UUID**: `ee5aacad-f05c-4d19-82b9-e69cb1854b29`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `CRITICAL`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-28 22:54:51 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-28 22:54:51 UTC`

#### Description

Feedback on the latest change to route off sheet connectors for power and ground toward the top and bottom of the sheet:
- The off sheet connectors should stop short when encountering other obstacles. In the attached screenshot, all 3 GND connectors and routing intersect with tables and component sections 
- C8 and Q1 are huge! Can we change all the discrete component formatting sot hey are sized the same as C6 on the same sheet?
- On sheet 8, pull up routing to 3V3 has stage antennas to either side of the off sheet "3V3" symbol. Screenshot attached!
- There are multiple overlaps on sheet 17. The sheet needs to be broken into multiple sub sheets (maybe 4 should work) and all of the symbol overlaps should be resolved
- Can we update the DRC engine for schematic sheets to check if text is overlapping? There is pretty prominent text overlap on this sheet. Screenshot attached
- The LED and jumper footprints on sheet 17 have overlapping text for pin labels to either side. Pins 1 and 2 for both the LED and jumper should be moved to the same side.
- The LED_AUD_K and LED_PERIPH_K text on sheet 17 is outside of the sheet border.
- On sheet 17, R7-R12 symbols are huge! please make them smaller and fix whatever is causing huge discrete components symbols to be created.

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1790636178362.png](attachments/pasted_screenshot_1790636178362.png) | Pasted screenshot |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1790636255586.png](attachments/pasted_screenshot_1790636255586.png) | Pasted screenshot |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1790636366486.png](attachments/pasted_screenshot_1790636366486.png) | Pasted screenshot |

#### Resolution Notes

- **Obstacle Avoidance**: Constructed `obstacle_boxes` in `src/provider/schematic_diagram.py` combining component bounding boxes, title block (`202.0, 12.0, 83.0, 32.0`), decoupling card, and truth tables. Vertical GND and power trunks dynamically query obstacles and stop short with safe margins instead of cutting through tables or title blocks.
- **Discrete Component Sizing**: Standardized discrete symbol dimensions in `schematic_diagram.py`: horizontal resistor zig-zag width reduced from 20.0mm to 8.0mm (`r_half_w = 4.0`), amplitude to +/-1.6mm; capacitor plate height reduced from 15.0mm to 7.0mm (`plate_h = 3.5`), matching C6 in the decoupling capacitor bank; transistor Q1 gate and channel bars scaled down to 7.0mm and 9.0mm.
- **Pullup Stage Antennas**: Terminated pull-up vertical wire segments at `y_top_rail = y_zz_top + 6.0` in `src/provider/schematic/passives.py`, matching the horizontal crossbar and eliminating top rail overshoot stubs.
- **Sheet 17 Sub-Sheet Split**: Replaced dense single sheet with 4 clean sub-sheets in `pcb.yaml`:
  - Sheet 17: Status and Overrides - MCU Reset & Bootloader (SW1, JP1, JP2)
  - Sheet 18: Status and Overrides - Power Isolation & Boot Mode (JP3, JP4)
  - Sheet 19: Status and Overrides - Primary Power LEDs (D2, D3, D4, R7, R8, R9)
  - Sheet 20: Status and Overrides - Peripheral & MCU LEDs (D5, D6, D7, R10, R11, R12)
- **Pin Side Configuration**: Configured `pin_sides: {'1': left, '2': left}` for JP1-JP4 and D2-D7, eliminating right-side pin collisions between adjacent components.
- **Schematic DRC Text Overlap Check**: Added `compute_text_bounding_boxes` to `SchematicBoundingBoxCalculator` and `SchematicDiagram`, and integrated `SCHEMATIC_TEXT_COLLISION` and `SCHEMATIC_PAGE_BOUNDARY_EXCEEDED` checks in `PCBDesignRulesChecker.check_schematic`.
- **Wire Routing in Same-Column**: Updated `SchematicWireSegmentPlanner` in `src/provider/schematic/wire_router.py` to route collinear vertical connections directly without redundant loopbacks.
- **Regression Unit Test**: Added `test_regression_bug_206_off_sheet_schematic_feedback` in `src/tests/test_pcb_advanced.py`.

#### Description

Clicking on any PR past PR535 in the dashboard results in a 404 error.

#### Resolution Notes

1. Added `get_remote_pr_numbers()` in `GitEngine` (`src/provider/vcs/git_engine.py`) to query remote repository pull request heads via `ls-remote origin refs/pull/*/head` and cache the set of verified pull requests existing on GitHub.
2. In `_extract_pr_info()`, validated PR numbers extracted from local branch tags against remote pull requests: unsubmitted local PR branches (e.g. `pr535`..`pr540`) resolve to `pr_status = 'Local PR #<num>'` with `pr_url = None` to prevent generating 404 URLs.
3. Updated `get_branch_url()` to route uncreated PR branches to `/tree/<branch>` rather than non-existent `/pull/<num>` URLs.
4. Rendered `.pr-local-badge` styling in `src/provider/templates/diff_view.html.j2` with local fallback toast handlers on PR and branch badges.
5. In `onBranchBadgeClick()`, guarded PR URL opening by verifying `isRemote` status before navigating to GitHub pull requests.
6. Added dedicated regression unit test `test_regression_bug_212_pr_past_535_404_handling` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

### <a id="bug-214"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-214]` Remove PCIe end connector, add support for BTLE

- **UUID**: `8f70dffb-8217-429e-a877-6eca66f8a4b7`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `LOW`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board, enclosure_bottom`
- **Created**: `2026-09-29 02:33:47 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-29 17:54:33 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-29 17:54:33 UTC`

#### Description

-Remove the PCIe connector and cutout from the design, there is no use case for it.
-Add support for BTLE to function as a UART connected to U1
-Minimum speed: 1Mb/s
-Support pairing by a cap touch input gesture, or proximity-based pairing (similar to AirPods)
-Antennae should be built into PCB, an external antenna is acceptable if required by design constraints. If we are adding an external antenna, the enclosure needs to be modified with an antenna mount
-Main user LED and piezo buzzer will provide the BTLE connection status information
-Bluetooth logo should be visible on the enclosure cover
-Ensure PCI and schematic design is updated

#### Resolution Notes

Removed PCIe J1 connector and enclosure cutouts; integrated u-blox NINA-B302 U11 BTLE module with 1Mb/s UART interface, capacitive touch pairing, status LED/buzzer signaling, Bluetooth runic logo on enclosure lid, complete PCB/schematic integration, updated downselection reports and carrier board documentation, and pruned dead M.2 settings.

---

### <a id="bug-216"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-216]` Bugs reopened after clicking "Save and Exit" in dashboard

- **UUID**: `dfdd9e04-21aa-4b61-a385-91cd637e5310`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `CRITICAL`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-09-29 03:18:46 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-29 03:18:46 UTC`

#### Description

I clicked "Save and Exit" in the dashboard and a bunch of extra bugs appeared. I am not sure why, see the tracebacks below.

#### Resolution Notes

1. Started background file watcher thread unconditionally in `BugReportServer.__init__` so embedded bug server in `DashboardServer` actively detects changes in `feedback/`.
2. Fixed `/api/version` in `DashboardServer` to return the integer `db_version` counter so client-side `pollForExternalUpdates()` detects changes, and updated `/api/next_bug_id` to return `{"next_id": ...}` matching client expectations.
3. Added file watch checks to `save_and_sync()`, `/api/exit`, and mutating requests in `do_POST` so changes on disk are merged before saving.
4. Protected `RESOLVED` bug states from regressions across `merge_databases()`, `scan_and_sync_feedback_dir()`, `_handle_save_bug()`, and `export_individual_bug()`, preventing unrefreshed UI form submissions or stale markdown exports from wiping resolution notes or reopening issues.
5. Added automated regression test `test_regression_bug_216_save_and_exit_preserves_resolved_bugs` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

---

### <a id="bug-217"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-217]` Add horizontal and vertical resizes to bug report page

- **UUID**: `3c74cb99-5099-494d-bb4f-50d774189cf1`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `dashboard`
- **Created**: `2026-09-29 03:20:15 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-29 03:20:15 UTC`

#### Description

Add horizontal and vertical resizers to text controls in the bug report page, and automatically increase the vertical size (up to a limit) of text controls as more information is filled in.

#### Resolution Notes

1. Added `resize: both !important;` to all `textarea` elements in `src/provider/templates/bug_report.html.j2`, with `min-width: 200px` and `max-width: 100%`, enabling bidirectional manual resizing.
2. Added `resize: horizontal;` to `input[type="text"]` elements with `min-width: 150px` and `max-width: 100%`.
3. Implemented `autoResizeTextarea(el, maxLimit=500)` in client-side JavaScript, calculating scroll height and dynamically adjusting element height up to a 500px limit, switching to scroll overflow when exceeding the ceiling.
4. Hooked global `input` event listener to dynamically expand textareas as information is entered, and hooked `loadActiveBug()`, `init()`, and `toggleExpandPanel()` to automatically adjust heights upon bug selection.
5. Added automated regression test `test_regression_bug_217_textarea_bidirectional_and_autoresize` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

### <a id="bug-218"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-218]` Error creating PR

- **UUID**: `86f947d2-9a83-4e3d-955a-3a9849bd3ecd`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `dashboard`
- **Created**: `2026-09-29 04:03:57 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-29 04:03:57 UTC`

#### Description

When I try to create a PR for the commit 4bc4bf09 I get the associated error in "Execution Logs and Tracebacks". If a PR already merged the commit into the tracking branch, can we hide the commit in the VCS window by default?

#### Resolution Notes

1. Updated `GitEngine.create_prs_for_commits` in `src/provider/vcs/git_engine.py` to use `git branch -a --points-at <commit>` instead of `--contains`, preventing ancestor commits from false-positive conflict detections with PR branches pointing to descendant commits.
2. Added detection of upstream tracking branch (`@{upstream}`, `origin/main`, `main`) in `GitEngine.get_smartlog_dag` and flagged merged commits using `is_merged` and `is_merged_into_tracking` fields on `CommitNodeModel`.
3. Updated PR creation to cleanly reject attempts to create PRs for commits already merged into the tracking branch.
4. Added `#smartlogList.hide-merged` styling and default hidden state in `src/provider/templates/diff_view.html.j2`, tagging merged nodes with `.merged-commit` and adding a `✓ Merged` badge (`.node-badge-merged`).
5. Added `btnToggleMerged` button in the Smartlog header with localStorage persistence (`diffview_hide_merged`) allowing users to toggle merged commit visibility on demand.
6. Added automated regression test `test_regression_bug_218_pr_creation_points_at_and_merged_commits_hidden` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

### <a id="bug-220"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-220]` Unexpected isolation results in flying probes test

- **UUID**: `6ceab5bc-759a-49af-96a5-314d89eefa4e`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `flex_tail`
- **Created**: `2026-09-29 04:15:04 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-29 04:15:04 UTC`

#### Description

Flying probes test- there's a bunch of isolation test results that are included for the flex tail that shouldn't be possible to test. Pasted into Tracebacks section below

#### Reproduction Steps

1. $ python src/view.py  carrier_board/flex_tail:view/simulate

#### Resolution Notes

1. Updated `verify_signal_lines_isolation` in `src/provider/simulation/flying_probe.py` to accept `subassembly: Optional[str] = None` and return empty isolation checks when inspecting `flex_tail`, as the flexible tail lacks opposing test pads or local DC power/ground reference test points for galvanic isolation probing.
2. Updated `create_flying_probe_hooks` in `src/provider/simulation/flying_probe.py` to pass `subassembly=target_label` and filter `board_comp_names` so that `flex_tail` simulation only loads test steps explicitly defined for `flex_tail` in `pcb_test_steps.yaml` (7 capacitive and continuity steps), omitting nonexistent `TEST_ISO_*` steps.
3. Verified `render_markdown_test_report` omits the `Signal Line Isolation Audit` section when `isolation_checks` is empty, while correctly rendering `Mutual Capacitance Touch Simulation & Verification (Flex Tail)`.
4. Added automated regression unit test `test_regression_bug_220_flex_tail_flying_probe_isolation_excluded` in `src/projects/tests/test_carrier_board.py`.

---

#### Resolution Notes

Updated `GitEngine.get_branches` in `src/provider/vcs/git_engine.py` to query both `refs/heads/` and `refs/remotes/`, and strip `refs/heads/` prefix directly from the full reference name rather than using ambiguous `%(refname:short)`, ensuring `refs/heads/main` resolves cleanly to `main` even when a colliding tag named `main` exists.

4. Updated branch classification and sorting in `src/provider/templates/diff_view.html.j2` so `main` is placed first, followed by release branches `v1..v6` sorted numerically in the `⭐ Main & Release Branches` section.
5. Added automated regression test `test_regression_bug_221_branches_missing_from_branch_viewer` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

### <a id="bug-231"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-231]` Our BLE module requires firmware to work

- **UUID**: `ecc5b869-b081-4c35-b6e8-efa828907873`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `CRITICAL`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-09-29 19:52:14 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-29 22:10:32 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-29 22:10:32 UTC`

#### Description

According to the data sheet our BLE module NINA-B302-00B comes unflashed, we should use the flashed NINA-B312 variant, and include an SWD header as a recovery step. I have also noted that the PCB footprint does not match the board footprint and the NINA module will intersect with the side of the carrier enclosure, so we may need to move this component to the other side of the board and relate test points TP2-TP8 to place it correctly within the PCB's confines.

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1790711704163.png](attachments/pasted_screenshot_1790711704163.png) | Pasted screenshot |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1790711777076.png](attachments/pasted_screenshot_1790711777076.png) | Pasted screenshot |
| `document` | [u-blox_NINA-B30_datasheet.pdf](attachments/u-blox_NINA-B30_datasheet.pdf) | Uploaded document u-blox_NINA-B30_datasheet.pdf |

#### Resolution Notes

Replaced U11 with pre-flashed NINA-B312-02B, added SWD recovery header J15 at (-14.5, -41.0), updated footprint to LGA-72 Table 27, and eliminated all DRC violations.

#### Description

I see "CR_working.md" in the feedback directory. When we commit changes through the VCS, we should precompute the commit hash to rename this file correctly:

```
# 1. Store the stash's commit hash into a variable
STASH_HASH=$(git rev-parse stash@{0})

# 2. Pop the stash to bring your files back into your working directory
git stash pop

# 3. Rename the file using the stored hash
mv CR_feedback.md "CR_${STASH_HASH}.md"

# 4. Amend renamed feedback file
git commit -a
```

#### Resolution Notes

Auto-rename CR_working.md to CR_<commit_sha>.md on git commit

Sheet 2 shows a Q1 transistor going to a VLOAD_SW on the NINA. VLOAD_SW has no pin marker, and there is no VLOAD_SW in the NINA docs. ### <a id="bug-250"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-250]` NINA-Utilize Native nRF52840 NFC on the NINA-B312

- **UUID**: `e025c345-f40a-4667-b334-1438060c52ce`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-09-30 20:23:38 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-09-30 21:33:52 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-09-30 21:33:52 UTC`

#### Description

┃   The u-blox NINA-B312 module is based on the Nordic Semiconductor nRF52840 SoC, which features an
 ┃   integrated NFC-A Type 2 / Type 4 Tag peripheral with hardware touch-to-wake support.
 ┃ 
 ┃   • Hardware Requirements:
 ┃       • Route the NFC1 and NFC2 pins from the NINA-B312 module footprint to an external 13.56 MHz tuned coil
 ┃       antenna.
 ┃       • Place two external tuning shunt capacitors (C_{tune1}, C_{tune2}, typically 180--330 pF NPO/C0G)
 ┃       across NFC1/NFC2 to match the target antenna loop inductance to resonance at 13.56 MHz (f =
 ┃       1/(2π√(L_{ant}C_{tot}))).
 ┃   • Pros: Zero additional active ICs, zero added quiescent current, and native Nordic SDK / Zephyr / Embassy
 ┃   firmware driver support.

#### Resolution Notes

Routed native nRF52840 NFC1/NFC2 from U11 (NINA-B312) to external tuned coil antenna header J16 with 300pF C0G shunt tuning capacitors C18 and C19, achieving 0 DRC violations.

### <a id="bug-258"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-258]` CR feedback- keeps showing up as modified, only timestamp is updated

- **UUID**: `2a63217e-7735-4666-bb34-2d0227427918`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-10-01 23:45:01 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-02 00:23:51 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-02 00:23:51 UTC`

#### Description

I'm not able to go to any ancestor commit right now; something keeps modifying CR feedback timestamps. I tried amending the change already, but the problem keeps coming back

#### Execution / Console Logs

```text
$ sl co 8e1f2fbd
abort: Command exited with code 1
  git --git-dir=/Users/<username>/gh/hardware/.git checkout -d --recurse-submodules 8e1f2fbdfe7a566a0f5afc196715a90d1b81a424
    error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by checkout:
        feedback/CR_04a83d62459e19ef0a47878543121542b83797da.md
    Please commit your changes or stash them before you switch branches.
    Aborting

(cq) 
$ sl status
M feedback/CR_04a83d62459e19ef0a47878543121542b83797da.md

# The repository is in an unfinished *update* state.
# To continue:                sl co 8e1f2fbd
# To abort:                   sl goto . --clean    (warning: this will discard uncommitted changes)
(cq) 
$ sl goto . --clean
update complete
(cq) 
$ sl status
M feedback/CR_04a83d62459e19ef0a47878543121542b83797da.md
(cq)
```

#### Resolution Notes

Prevent timestamp-only rewrites of code review markdown reports (CR.md and CR_<commit>.md) when findings and comments have not changed; preserve existing Review Date and commit-specific file counts.

### <a id="bug-259"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-259]` Carrier board schematic feedback-floating pins, component spacing, off sheet connectors

- **UUID**: `a5d1dd65-97d5-46f7-aeb5-42bb81e7f45a`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-10-01 23:47:10 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-02 01:15:53 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-02 01:15:53 UTC`

#### Description

Sheet 3: BYP on U10 shows up as floating
Sheet 4: Pin D1 on U1 shows up as floating
Sheet 8: VREGD and VREGA- off sheet connectors placed here, but not used elsewhere in the sheet?
Sheet 10: EGP/GND on U11 shows up as floating
Sheet 11: J15 and SW2- can we move them to the middle of the sheet?
Can we remove these unused pins from the schematic or route them appropriately, and address all other schematic formatting issues

#### Resolution Notes

Resolved floating pins on U10 (BYP) and U1 (D1) by removing unused pins from Sheet 3 and 4 breakouts. Removed dangling off-sheet connectors for VREGD and VREGA on Sheet 8 U2, added *VREG* to POWER_NET_PATTERNS and grouped decoupling caps by power net to prevent cross-rail bridging. Refined allowed_pins matching in schematic diagram and DRC to prevent false label matching of secondary ground pins (EGP, GND_12, GND_26, GND_30) on U11. Updated cols_override layout spacing to honor col_gap and center components horizontally and vertically on Sheet 11 (J15, SW2).

---

### <a id="bug-260"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-260]` Schematic Index-sheet names fall of edge of page

- **UUID**: `7214bbbe-ebcd-4f3e-a535-521545de99b6`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `LOW`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-10-02 01:05:52 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-02 01:25:32 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-02 01:25:32 UTC`

#### Description

The sheet names fall off the edge of the page-see screenshot below. We may simply abbreviate/truncate the sheet names on the index to prevent this issue from occuring

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `screenshot` | [pasted_screenshot_1790903212489.png](attachments/pasted_screenshot_1790903212489.png) | Pasted screenshot |

#### Resolution Notes

Constrained Table of Contents Document Structure entry lengths to MAX_ENTRY_LEN (95 chars) and only included parenthetical descriptions if the combined line fits within the margin. Added a fail-safe truncation during TOC rendering so lines never exceed page borders. Added regression test test_regression_bug_260_schematic_index_sheet_names_fit_page.

### <a id="bug-261"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-261]` Downselection report-feedback

- **UUID**: `3e4ffc46-5e7d-45e2-a3b8-f72a74b20d06`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-10-02 01:11:46 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-02 01:35:39 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-02 01:35:39 UTC`

#### Description

We should include the following data in supplier PCB docs in the future, can you update our docs to include:
-min track spacing in mils
-min hole size
-for rigid-flex type, supplier requests information for both the rigid part and the flexible part in the same order
-special requirements-unless excluded from SMT/PCB assembly best practices, exclude from documentation
-Detailed Assembly & SMT Process Guidelines - can you remove special formatting from this and limit to 600 chars

#### Resolution Notes

Updated supplier PCB review deck to include minimum track spacing in mils (4.72 mil rigid, 5.91 mil flex), minimum hole size (6.30 mil microvia, 9.84 mil via), standard rigid-then-flex column ordering, plain text formatting in Detailed Assembly & SMT Process Guidelines, and removed redundant MSL 3 bakeout callouts.

### <a id="bug-262"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-262]` Supplier PCB guidelines

- **UUID**: `1f8e5ea0-c7ef-47e7-9af4-445c643191ea`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Created**: `2026-10-02 01:35:53 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-02 01:49:00 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-02 01:49:00 UTC`

#### Description

Each project should output supplier files:
-gerbers.zip: contains .pcb .pcbdoc .cam .brd and gerber files
-bom_templates.zip: contains <PCB name>_bom.csv BOM list for each PCB
-centroid_files.zip: contains <PCB name>_pos.csv centroid list for each PCB
-assembly_files.zip: contains <PCB name>_top.png, <PCB name>_bottom.png top and bottom PCB textures for each PCB
The zip files should go under build/board

#### Resolution Notes

Added Builder.package_supplier_pcb_files to automatically package supplier zip archives under build/board and build/board/<project>: gerbers.zip (contains .pcb, .pcbdoc, .cam, .brd, and all gerber files), bom_templates.zip (contains <PCB name>_bom.csv for each PCB), centroid_files.zip (contains <PCB name>_pos.csv for each PCB), and assembly_files.zip (contains <PCB name>_top.png and <PCB name>_bottom.png textures for each PCB). Added regression test test_regression_bug_262_supplier_pcb_guidelines_zip_outputs.

### <a id="bug-265"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-265]` Simplify build logging

- **UUID**: `17d15352-0155-46fa-9467-e6674b8b0f6e`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `GENERAL`
- **Component**: `build`
- **Created**: `2026-10-02 02:17:45 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-02 02:47:18 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-02 02:47:18 UTC`

#### Description

Can we simplify the logging of tools long these lines-
-Only log what target got built to stdout
-Use structured logging to log individual file compilations to build/daemon.log
Example below

We could extrapolate this further to all tools. For example, in the new scheme view.py should only show the target being shown, and everything else would be output to daemon.log:

$ python src/view.py carrier_board/carrier_board:pcb
👁️ Showing carrier_board_carrier_board_pcb 
▶ + 
✔ Done Visualizing...

$ python src/view.py carrier_board/carrier_board:pcb
👁️ Showing carrier_board_carrier_board_pcb 
✔ Done Visualizing...

#### Behavior Comparison

- **Expected**: $ python src/build.py "carrier_board/*"
- **Actual**: $ python src/build.py "carrier_board/*"

#### Resolution Notes

Route individual file compilation logs to build/daemon.log via Logger.log structured logging, keeping stdout clean with only target compilation summaries and completion status.

### <a id="bug-268"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-268]` I seem to have to rebuilt the carrier_board project to view PCB changes

- **UUID**: `5d067dd2-ff41-469f-b2ae-8e903496bfe9`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `GENERAL`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-10-02 03:32:34 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-02 03:55:26 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-02 03:55:26 UTC`

#### Description

This seems like a general build issue, but it repress easily for the carrier_board project. I need to rebuild the carrier_board project to view PCB changes. I placed example commands in expected/actual showing what command I want to run to view the updated PCB and what I actually have to run

#### Behavior Comparison

- **Expected**: $ python src/view.py carrier_board/carrier_board:pcb
- **Actual**: $ python src/build.py "carrier_board/*"

#### Attachments & References

| Type | Filename | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `document` | [daemon.log](attachments/daemon.log) | Uploaded document daemon.log |

#### Resolution Notes

Propagate all PCB configuration models (omitted_silkscreen_designators, silkscreen_graphics, design_rules, net_classes, schematic_sheets, revision) to pcb_cfg in view.py and target_cfg in build.py, ensuring view.py immediately exports and displays the latest PCB changes without requiring build.py first.

Encode attachments scoped by bug ID under attachments/<bug_id>/<filename>, preventing collisions when multiple bugs share identical attachment filenames while maintaining Git LFS tracking and HTTP serving.

### <a id="bug-272"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-272]` W908185ASE67-Supplier feedback

- **UUID**: `861c6a43-d2ce-4f49-967e-0c7f161bf7ba`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `carrier_board`
- **Created**: `2026-10-04 16:45:58 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-04 17:03:12 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-04 17:03:12 UTC`

#### Description

1. Which soldermask color is correct?
2. You've chosen impedance control, could you please include impedance control info (track width/spacing, value, position/layer) in file?
3. It has vias on SMD pads and it has no plug vias in BGA area, suggest fill all vias with resin and cap, is it okay?

#### Resolution Notes

1. Solder Mask Color: Confirmed Matte Black (with White silkscreen and ENIG finish). Synchronized manifest.yaml color to [0.12, 0.12, 0.12, 1.0], emitted solder mask in KiCad stackup, and enabled --use-board-stackup-colors for photorealistic Matte Black assembly textures. 2. Controlled Impedance: Embedded controlled impedance specification table in project_summary.txt, project_summary.md, impedance_control_info.txt (in gerbers.zip), order remarks, and Dwgs.User drawing layer (50 Ohm SE L1 w=0.18mm ref L2; 90 Ohm diff L1 w=0.16mm s=0.18mm ref L2; 85 Ohm diff L1 w=0.18mm s=0.15mm ref L2). 3. Via Process: Confirmed YES to filling all vias in BGA area and SMD pads with non-conductive epoxy resin and capping/plating over per IPC-4761 Type VII (VIPPO).

### <a id="bug-280"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-280]` Remediations for stuck CI tasks

- **UUID**: `613d04a9-a148-4b93-9649-ab583808ad05`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `CI`
- **Created**: `2026-10-08 19:52:26 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-08 20:03:46 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-08 20:03:46 UTC`

#### Description

We need to implement the following remediations for stuck CI tasks:

  ### Recommended Remediation

  #### A. Terminate the Build Daemon in ci-gate.yml or Pass --no-daemon

  To prevent orphan daemon processes from keeping the runner host alive, ensure the daemon is cleanly stopped or bypassed in CI:

          - name: Run Smoke Tests
            shell: bash -el {0}
            env:
              PYTHONPATH: src
            run: |
              set -o pipefail
              python src/smoke.py
              python src/daemon.py stop || true

  Alternatively, in smoke.py:37-41, automatically append --no-daemon when executing build.py or view.py so no background processes
  are spawned.

  #### B. Add a SIGTERM Handler to daemon.py

  Register signal handlers so daemon.py exits immediately when the runner sends SIGTERM:

    import signal

    def handle_sigterm(signum, frame):
        sys.exit(0)

    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, handle_sigterm)

  #### C. Add Concurrency & Missing Event Triggers to ci-gate.yml

  Update the top of .github/workflows/ci-gate.yml:

    name: CI Gate Validation
    on:
      pull_request:
        types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true

#### Resolution Notes

Implemented concurrency cancellation and ready_for_review triggers in ci-gate.yml, added --no-daemon auto-injection in smoke.py, and added SIGTERM graceful shutdown in daemon.py

### <a id="bug-translucent-tapeworm-953"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-TRANSLUCENT-TAPEWORM-953]` Dashboard stuck at 20% on launch

- **UUID**: `3e17a613-50d8-4c90-9e62-24e63b8f13fe`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `dashboard`
- **Created**: `2026-10-15 00:32:11 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-15 00:32:17 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-15 00:32:17 UTC`

#### Description

Upon launching or restarting the dashboard workstation, the UI was stuck displaying the feedback database synchronization modal at 20% progress. Inspection revealed a JavaScript `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` in `diff_view.html.j2:1705` within the `sanitizeAuthor()` function introduced during privacy sanitization hardening. Because the script failed to parse, `initDiffView()` and `performInitialSync()` never ran, leaving the modal stuck at its initial 20% HTML state.

#### Resolution Notes

1. Pruned dangling closing parenthesis in `sanitizeAuthor()` condition in `src/provider/templates/diff_view.html.j2`.
2. Hardened workstation initialization lifecycle so `initDiffView()` fires immediately if `document.readyState !== 'loading'`, eliminating dependency on potentially pre-fired `DOMContentLoaded` events.
3. Added comprehensive regression test `test_regression_bug_translucent_tapeworm_953_dashboard_js_syntax_and_sync_screen` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py` verifying balanced syntax and executing `node -c` across extracted `<script>` blocks in all dashboard templates (`diff_view.html.j2`, `code_review.html.j2`, `bug_report.html.j2`).

---

### <a id="bug-loamy-bristle-455"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-LOAMY-BRISTLE-455]` Elide physical address and personal email in privacy sanitizer

- **UUID**: `09c3136e-35c6-442e-9708-46ac711fa0ed`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `sanitizer`
- **Created**: `2026-10-15 00:37:10 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-15 00:37:11 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-15 00:37:11 UTC`

#### Description

Extend the zero-dependency personal privacy and identity sanitizer (`src/provider/sanitizer.py`) to systematically redact physical addresses (street names, numbers, suite/apt/unit designators, P.O. Boxes, and postal/ZIP codes) and personal email addresses (user handles, consumer email domains like `@gmail.com`, `@me.com`, etc.) across developer feedback, bug reports, and logs. Additionally, update VCS engine commit author and email mapping to redact user author identities to `User` and `user@workspace`.

#### Resolution Notes

1. Added physical street address, unit/suite, and P.O. Box regex redaction to `<address>` and `<zip>` in `elide_personal_info()`, using pure regex matching without requiring an engineering whitelist or supplier address preservation.
2. Dynamically discovered user emails, handles, and system usernames to map all personal identifiers and consumer email domains to `<email>`.
3. Updated `elide_commit_author()` and `elide_commit_email()` in `src/provider/sanitizer.py` to map user author identities and commit emails to `User` and `user@workspace` via dynamic discovery.
4. Updated VCS workstation frontend `sanitizeAuthor()` in `diff_view.html.j2` and `code_review.html.j2` to read the author blacklist dynamically from the backend session.
5. Added dedicated regression unit tests in `src/tests/test_privacy_and_relative_paths.py`.

### <a id="bug-hairy-wasp-932"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-HAIRY-WASP-932]` Update TMC6300 wiring to 6-PWM GPIO control and decouple SEN pin (WORM-GLIDING-BRISTLE-252)

- **UUID**: `146f6268-0981-4761-ad81-d040b71ecedb`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `PCB`
- **Component**: `cat_fountain`
- **Created**: `2026-10-15 21:12:56 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-15 21:22:37 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-15 21:22:37 UTC`

#### Description

TMC6300 3-phase BLDC driver in cat_fountain requires 6 independent PWM/GPIO inputs (UH, UL, VH, VL, WH, WL) for proper 3-phase commutation. Disconnect the bridged inputs (IN1, IN2, IN3) and allocate GP16..GP21 for 6-PWM control (UH=GP16, UL=GP17, VH=GP18, VL=GP19, WH=GP20, WL=GP21) with DIAG on GP22. The TMC6300 breakout SEN pin (intended for attaching an analog current monitor) is left disconnected from MCU GPIO/ADC in favor of dedicated INA219 current monitoring on the 5V boost rail. Preserve the AH3577 Hall speed sensor on GP26 for contactless impeller rotation speed monitoring.

#### Resolution Notes

Reconfigured TMC6300 motor driver wiring to 6-PWM GPIO control across GP16..GP21 (UH, UL, VH, VL, WH, WL) with DIAG on GP22. Left the breakout's SEN pin decoupled from MCU GPIO/ADC as motor current monitoring is performed over I2C by the INA219 sensor. Preserved the AH3577 Hall speed sensor and speed_sense net on GP26. Updated RP2040 GPIO key and TMC6300 pin key definitions, and added regression test coverage.

---

#### Resolution Notes

Removed redundant and useless shallow regression test wrappers that only wrapped other test suites or cargo tests. Codified regression test best practice rules in GEMINI.md across firmware and hardware repos, prohibiting shallow test wrappers, requiring direct updates to original test cases, and preferring omission when logical invariants are already verified.

### <a id="bug-vibrant-woodborer-940"></a> 🟢 `[BUG-VIBRANT-WOODBORER-940]` Create motor hub assembly

- **UUID**: `c90ede81-7e1b-4c52-9ff2-529904ec722a`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `HIGH`
- **Category**: `CAD`
- **Component**: `cat_fountain`
- **Created**: `2026-10-23 22:54:57 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-10-24 01:29:24 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-10-24 01:29:24 UTC`

#### Description

Right now debugging motor issues is very difficult. Can we pls create a motor hub assembly which combines the hall sensor, motor, drive hub, and motor clip into a single subassembly unit which clips into the bottom of the bowl and interfaces magnetically with the impeller? See this additional feedback for more optimizations and improvements:

1. Center the Thrust Bearing (Reduce Friction Radius by 90%):
      • Remove the outer perimeter standoff ring on the drive hub at R = 15.6 mm.
      • Add a small PTFE (Teflon) thrust washer or tiny acetal/POM button directly around the 1.5 mm motor shaft collar at R ≤ 1.5
      mm.
      • Dropping the contact radius from 15.6 mm down to 1.5 mm reduces friction torque by over 90% (T_f ∝ R).

2. Optimize Magnetic Coupling Strength:
      • Increase the axial air gap from 1.5 mm to 2.0--2.5 mm. Magnetic attraction drops with 1/d² while rotational
      magnetic coupling torque remains sufficient for fluid pumping.

3. Speed Sensor Pocket Alignment:
      • Ensure that the Hall sensor pocket at Y = 18.5 mm directly aligns with the drive hub's magnet pitch circle so the Hall
      sensor receives strong alternating pulses to reliably output SPEED_SENSE (GP26). 
      • These are the hall sensors I purchased: 

https://www.amazon.com/FORIOT-Effect-Sensor-3144E-A3144/dp/B0H69BSJ4Z/ref=sr_1_4_pp?crid=ZUG52D2UM8C&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.lpKwwD9zXT4MytW_o1867YiT79Yl-lsXrO86wfgsgnShDxXo1Ptvdg432J9RLfUlPqg3sgQwgI4ajloN9FG2Zlo3KyUWIIIhG1epfbhZ8rnOzwoVy8yOpe6GIQNE5Si866q-1S70Y6wKyFPuvuxLJ8Qlbu4LJdNtf5Sjqjq45d-qswe8QjFcGbVlpS3Cpaxq770C7UN_pKv_ssgpbkmEzIl_EmazNDYryvgi4d-H-38.jt36wv_LPOYxzl2HI64T4n84lfvUbY3Z5gwIZfFs2bI&dib_tag=se&keywords=hall+sensor&qid=1792796296&sprefix=hall+senso%2Caps%2C183&sr=8-4

     • They are standard A3144 hall sensors which are mounted on PCBs and include mounting holes. I am able to bend the hall sensor off the PCB to vary its pitch, but the effective height is a few mm shorter than a standalone hall sensor.
 
4. Update the cat fountain docs with needed BOM updates

#### Resolution Notes

Replaced motor_clip and integrated enclosed well beneath the impeller with dedicated motor drive hub assembly (motor_hub) sliding into guide tracks on bowl base, while keeping drive_hub as separate rotating drive unit so motor and drive hub install and remove as a single unit without detaching.

- **UUID**: `4bfee9c3-96a6-4d79-b0f8-5e450e99fece`
- **Status**: `CLOSED`
- **Severity**: `MEDIUM`
- **Category**: `INFRASTRUCTURE`
- **Component**: `dashboard`
- **Created**: `2026-11-06 06:45:37 UTC`
- **Resolved**: `2026-11-06 17:13:20 UTC`
- **Accepted**: `2026-11-06 17:13:22 UTC`

#### Description

Repo actions like sync, and bug actions like saving, approving or rejecting, and creating bugs now take sufficiently long that I think we need a modal UI to show action status, similar to the UI used for creating PRs. Can we do some profiling of repo and bug actions, optimize if needed, and add modal progress UIs for actions that take sufficiently long (>1s)? The UIs should be hidden automatically after the action completes, and only show if the action is taking a long time. We can also make this change to the sync action to make all actions behave uniformly.

#### Attached Commits

- `64325f08`

#### Review Tasks & Functional Checklist

- [ ] <!-- task:c0f462e8 --> Inspect delayed (>1s) action progress modal on dashboard sync and bug workstation | `python tools/dashboard.py`

#### Resolution Notes

Added delayed (>1s) action progress modal with live elapsed timer to dashboard and bug workstation, and optimized incremental attachment indexing.

#### Description

Opening a commit in the bug report station doesn’t go to the code review window directly, instead it opens up a website to the toplevel VCS UI with only the working tree selected.
